aq1.text: After losing a match — what do you do?
aq1.a: I break down the mistakes and think about how to improve
aq1.b: I laugh it off and move on to the next game

aq2.text: When you're on the court — what are you thinking about?
aq2.a: Winning — I focus on tactics and the result
aq2.b: The energy and vibe with my partner

aq3.a: To push myself and test my limits
aq3.b: For fun and a break from work

aq4.text: Who do you prefer to play with?
aq4.a: People I already know and trust

aq5.a: To grow to a professional level
aq5.b: Padel is my hobby and entertainment

aq6.text: Before a match — how do you prepare?
aq6.a: I warm up for 10 minutes — it matters
aq6.b: I jump straight in — why wait?

lq1.text: Is it better to wait for the right moment before striking — even if that means missing a few balls?
lq1.hint: Tell me, when do you usually rush a shot?
lq1.correct: ✅ Correct! Patience is the key in padel.
lq1.wrong: 💡 In padel, rushing a shot is more often a mistake than a solution.

lq2.text: After a wall shot — should you immediately take position at the net?

lq3.text: When your partner makes a mistake — is it better to immediately tell them what they did wrong?

lq4.text: A full-power smash — always the best choice when the ball is high?

lq5.text: Three mistakes in a row is normal — no need to change your whole game plan?

lq6.text: Court position is more important than shot power?

lq7.text: Against weak opponents you can relax and stop thinking about tactics?

levelQuizResult.honestMessage: This is your level under ideal conditions. In real play it's harder: your partner affects half of all rallies, emotions aren't always stable, and technique under pressure works differently. Your working level is one step down. That's not bad — that's honest. This is exactly where real growth begins.

levelQuiz.howDoYouDo: How do you usually do it?

q1.label: Goal
q1.text: Why did you start playing padel?

q2.label: Motivation
q2.text: What matters more to you on the court?

q3.label: Ideal
q3.text: What does your ideal game look like?

q4.label: Shot
q4.text: When the ball is coming at you — is it better to wait for the right moment and then strike?

q5.label: Wall
q5.text: After a bounce off the wall — should you immediately take position at the net?

q6.label: Partner
q6.text: When your partner makes a mistake — is it better to immediately tell them what they did wrong?

q7.label: Smash
q7.text: A full-power smash — always the best choice when the ball is high?

q8.label: Mindset
q8.text: Three mistakes in a row — it's normal, no need to change the whole game plan?

q9.label: Position
q9.text: Court position is more important than shot power?

q10.label: Strategy
q10.text: Against weak opponents you can relax and not think about tactics?

levelDescriptions.D-: You're just starting out — the most exciting moment. Everything lies ahead.
levelDescriptions.D: You understand the basics of padel. A few key habits and growth will be noticeable.
levelDescriptions.D+: There's understanding, but instincts outrun logic. The foundation is being built now.
levelDescriptions.C-: Good foundation. A few details make a big difference.
levelDescriptions.C: You're thinking right. Stability under pressure is the goal.
levelDescriptions.C+: Strong player. The main challenge — finding worthy partners.
